# Controlling indexing

Day 2, 10:30 · John Mueller, Search Relations Team Lead · coverage: transcript, slides, video

Named on the title slide. The first recording stops mid-sentence at the closing slide; a second, independent recording covers the end of the talk (robots.txt and robots meta rules, robots meta tags and JavaScript).

## Claims

- **[Stage]** John Mueller noted that robots.txt is defined by an internet standard, RFC 9309, which Google's Gary Illyes co-authored.
  <br><sub>`D2-C050` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [How Google interprets the robots.txt specification](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/robots-txt/robots-txt-spec), [Robots Refresher: Future-proof Robots Exclusion Protocol](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/03/robots-future), [Formalizing the Robots Exclusion Protocol Specification](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2019/07/rep-id) · Repeats [D1-C512](D1-S07-how-google-interprets-robots-txt.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** John Mueller said there is currently no RFC that standardises robots meta tags, unlike robots.txt.
  <br><sub>`D2-C051` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · consistent with Google docs · [Robots Refresher: Future-proof Robots Exclusion Protocol](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2025/03/robots-future)</sub>

- **[Stage]** John Mueller encouraged attendees to help write a specification for robots meta tags, saying internet standards groups are made up of ordinary people and need only passion and a willingness to join the discussions.
  <br><sub>`D2-C052` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · Repeated by [D2-C217](D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** John Mueller opened with a true-or-false quiz slide asking whether robots meta tags can make a page more visible in Search results than having none, and later answered that the statement is true.
  > "You can use robots meta tags to be more visible in Search results than without robots meta tags."
  <br><sub>`D2-C053` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · consistent with Google docs · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag), [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover) · Used by `DEV-IDX-04`</sub>

- **[Slide]** The robots meta tag is a piece of HTML code in the head section of a page that gives search engine crawlers page-specific instructions.
  <br><sub>`D2-C054` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag) · Used by the glossary term *Robots meta tag*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's robots meta tag specification tells site owners to place the tag in the head section but notes that Google Search does not enforce that placement and also respects robots meta tags in the body of an HTML document.
  <br><sub>`D2-C055` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Controlling indexing · is the documentation · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag)</sub>

- **[Slide]** The primary function of the robots meta tag is to control how a page is indexed and shown in search results.
  <br><sub>`D2-C056` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag) · Used by the glossary term *Robots meta tag*</sub>

- **[Slide]** The robots meta tag is written as `<meta name="robots" content="rule1,rule2">`, or with the name googlebot instead of robots, with several rules separated by commas.
  <br><sub>`D2-C057` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag), [meta tags and attributes that Google supports](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/special-tags) · Used by the glossary term *Robots meta tag*</sub>

- **[Stage]** John Mueller said robots.txt does not control indexing, so robots meta tags are what site owners have to use to control it.
  <br><sub>`D2-C058` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [Introduction to robots.txt](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/intro), [Block Search indexing with noindex](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/block-indexing) · Extends [D1-C110](D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) · Used by the glossary term *robots.txt*</sub>

- **[Slide]** The robots meta rule all is the default value and does nothing: it places no restrictions on indexing the page or following its links, the same as having no robots meta tag, and it is not an instruction that search engines must index the page.
  > "This is the default value - it does nothing"
  <br><sub>`D2-C059` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag), [meta tags and attributes that Google supports](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/special-tags) · Used by `DEV-IDX-06`</sub>

- **[Slide]** The noindex robots rule tells Google not to show the page in search results.
  <br><sub>`D2-C061` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag), [Block Search indexing with noindex](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/block-indexing) · Used by `DEV-IDX-01`, the glossary term *noindex*</sub>

- **[Slide]** A slide named internal admin pages, temporary landing pages and thin content as typical use cases for the noindex rule.
  <br><sub>`D2-C062` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** The page-level nofollow robots rule tells search engines not to pass signals to any of the links on the page, which John Mueller called a weird and very broad rule that makes the page stand on its own.
  <br><sub>`D2-C063` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · consistent with Google docs · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag), [Evolving "nofollow" – new ways to identify the nature of links](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2019/09/evolving-nofollow-new-ways-to-identify) · Extended by [D2-C821](D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) · Used by `DEV-IDX-06`, the glossary term *nofollow*</sub>

- **[Stage]** John Mueller recommends rel=nofollow on individual links instead of the page-level nofollow robots rule, so a site can choose which links are useful and which are not.
  <br><sub>`D2-C064` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · consistent with Google docs · [Qualify your outbound links to Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/qualify-outbound-links), [Evolving "nofollow" – new ways to identify the nature of links](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2019/09/evolving-nofollow-new-ways-to-identify) · Used by `DEV-IDX-06`</sub>

- **[Stage]** John Mueller suspected that if robots meta tags were reinvented today, the page-level nofollow rule would probably not be part of them.
  <br><sub>`D2-C821` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · Extends [D2-C063](D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Audit robots meta tags set by templates and plug-ins: an explicit all rule does nothing and can go, while a page-level nofollow strips link signals from every link on the page and is better replaced by qualifying only the specific links that need it.
  <br><sub>`D2-C065` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Controlling indexing · Used by `DEV-IDX-06`</sub>

- **[Stage]** John Mueller said AI crawlers do not really know what to do with nofollow links, because they look at the content rather than building a link graph; he did not say whether he meant Google's AI systems, other AI crawlers or both.
  > "AI crawlers don't really know what to do with a nofollow link, because they're looking at the content"
  <br><sub>`D2-C066` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Analysis]** nofollow is a link-graph hint for search engines, not an access control: to keep AI crawlers away from content, use robots.txt rules for the specific crawlers; at Google, Google-Extended covers Gemini training and grounding, and the Search generative AI control covers AI Overviews and AI Mode.
  <br><sub>`D2-C067` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Controlling indexing · Extends [D1-C127](D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) · Extends [D1-C482](D1-S12-q-a.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** The robots rule none is equivalent to noindex plus nofollow, so a page that carries it will not show up in Search, provided Google can see the tag.
  <br><sub>`D2-C068` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag), [Block Search indexing with noindex](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/block-indexing) · Used by `DEV-IDX-06`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's robots meta tag specification says robots meta tags and X-Robots-Tag headers are found only when a URL is crawled, so the rules on a URL disallowed in robots.txt are never seen and are ignored.
  <br><sub>`D2-C069` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Controlling indexing · is the documentation · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag), [Block Search indexing with noindex](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/block-indexing) · Extends [D1-C106](D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) · Used by `DEV-IDX-01`, `DEV-IDX-03`, the glossary term *X-Robots-Tag*</sub>

- **[Slide]** The nosnippet rule stops Google from showing a text snippet or video preview for a page in search results, while the page's title is still shown.
  <br><sub>`D2-C070` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag), [Control your snippets in search results](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/snippet) · Used by `DEV-IDX-05`, the glossary term *nosnippet and data-nosnippet*</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's robots meta tag specification says that with nosnippet a static image thumbnail, if available, may still be shown when that results in a better user experience.

- **[Slide]** The nosnippet rule also prevents a page's content from being used as a direct input for AI Overviews and AI Mode in Search.

- **[Stage]** John Mueller said Google uses the snippet as a way of building AI Overviews and AI Mode answers, so if a page forbids a snippet, Google cannot use that snippet for them.
  > "we use the snippet as a way of building out the AI Overviews and the AI Mode answers"
  <br><sub>`D2-C073` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · consistent with Google docs · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag), [AI features and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features) · Extends [D1-C038](D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Extended by [D2-C727](D2-S23-how-does-the-index-look-like.md) · Used by `DEV-IDX-05`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Before adding nosnippet or a low max-snippet value, weigh the cost in AI features: both limit how much of the page AI Overviews and AI Mode can use, and John Mueller described those answers as built from snippets.

- **[Stage]** John Mueller said data-nosnippet is rarely needed but lets a site keep a specific piece of text, such as a business phone number, out of the snippet, so the page can still be found for it while searchers have to visit the page to see it.

- **[Stage]** The data-nosnippet attribute can be used on only a handful of HTML elements.

- **[Analysis]** To hide one detail, such as a phone number, a price or a direct answer, instead of the whole snippet, wrap it in data-nosnippet on a span, div or section in the server HTML and validate the HTML so that an unclosed element cannot hide the rest of the page from snippets.

- **[Stage]** The unavailable_after rule lets a page drop out of search results after a set date and time, which suits time-bound pages, though John Mueller said most sites do not use it.

- **[Slide]** John Mueller's slide said Search Console has very few indexing-like settings and listed the Search generative AI control as the one control in his talk that is not a meta tag.
  > "Very few "indexing-like" settings are in Search Console"
  <br><sub>`D2-C102` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Slide]** Setting the Search generative AI control in Search Console to exclude keeps a site's links and content out of Search generative AI features such as AI Overviews and AI Mode, so the site gets no traffic or impressions from them; include is the default.
  <br><sub>`D2-C103` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [Search generative AI control](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024?hl=en) · Repeats [D1-C030](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) · Extends [D1-C029](D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md) · Used by `DEV-IDX-10`</sub>

- **[Slide]** To be as visible as possible in Google, John Mueller's closing slide recommended the robots rules max-image-preview:large and max-snippet:-1.
  > "To be as visible as possible in Google, use: max-image-preview:large, max-snippet:-1"
  <br><sub>`D2-C104` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · consistent with Google docs · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag), [Discover and your website](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/google-discover) · Used by `DEV-IDX-04`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Set max-snippet:-1 and max-image-preview:large on every indexable template unless licensing requires otherwise, and check that no CMS, plug-in or CDN setting adds lower snippet or image preview limits by default.
  <br><sub>`D2-C105` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Controlling indexing · Used by `DEV-IDX-04`</sub>

- **[Slide]** A slide said robots meta rules can be added to a page's HTML with JavaScript, but doing so takes more time.
  <br><sub>`D2-C106` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · consistent with Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Extended by [D2-C853](D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-05`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's meta tags documentation recommends avoiding JavaScript to inject or change meta tags whenever possible and testing the implementation thoroughly when it must be used.
  <br><sub>`D2-C107` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Controlling indexing · is the documentation · [meta tags and attributes that Google supports](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/special-tags) · Used by `DEV-REN-05`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Removing a robots restriction such as noindex with JavaScript does not work, a slide said.
  > "But... it takes more time, and removing restrictions (like "noindex") doesn't work."
  <br><sub>`D2-C108` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · consistent with Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Extended by [D2-C852](D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-05`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Ship robots rules in the HTML the server sends and never rely on JavaScript to lift a noindex: Google may skip rendering a page that arrives with noindex, so the page can stay out of the index even if a script removes the tag later.
  <br><sub>`D2-C109` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Controlling indexing · Extended by [D2-C855](D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-05`</sub>

- **[Stage]** John Mueller said robots meta rules only work if robots.txt allows Google to fetch the page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C850` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag), [Block Search indexing with noindex](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/block-indexing) · Repeats [D1-C110](D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) · Used by `DEV-IDX-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** When robots.txt blocks a page, the page's content is not indexable but Google can still index its URL, John Mueller said.
  <br><sub>`D2-C851` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [Introduction to robots.txt](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/intro), [Block Search indexing with noindex](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/block-indexing) · Repeats [D2-C021](D2-S02-welcome-to-indexing-day.md) · Repeats [D1-C110](D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) · Used by `DEV-IDX-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** When Google finds a noindex rule in a page's HTML, it drops the page without even processing its JavaScript, so a script cannot switch the page back to indexable, John Mueller said.
  > "we will see the noindex and say, oh, we will get rid of this page; we won't even process the JavaScript"
  <br><sub>`D2-C852` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · consistent with Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Extends [D2-C108](D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-05`</sub>

- **[Stage]** John Mueller recommended putting robots meta tags directly in a page's HTML exactly as intended, and adding them with JavaScript only where that is not possible, as in a JavaScript web app.
  <br><sub>`D2-C853` · Day 2, Controlling indexing (John Mueller) · confirmed by Google docs · [meta tags and attributes that Google supports](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/special-tags), [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Extends [D2-C106](D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md) · Used by `DEV-REN-05`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's JavaScript SEO basics guide says that when Google encounters a noindex rule it may skip rendering and JavaScript execution, so using JavaScript to change or remove a noindex robots meta tag may not work as expected.
  > "it may skip rendering and JavaScript execution"
  <br><sub>`D2-C854` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, Controlling indexing · is the documentation · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics) · Used by `DEV-REN-05`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** On stage the rule was absolute (Google won't even process the JavaScript of a page served with noindex), while Google's guide says only that it may skip rendering; either way, a noindex in the served HTML must never be one that JavaScript is expected to lift.
  <br><sub>`D2-C855` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Controlling indexing · Extends [D2-C109](D2-S04-controlling-indexing.md)</sub>
